subject.title: Feature: trustedWebhooks for Discord — allow specific webhooks to trigger agent responses

question: Should Discord gain a guild-scoped trusted webhook allowlist, and if so may trusted webhook messages map onto configured Discord user identities?
rationale: The requested allowlist is narrower than `allowBots: true`, but it would make possession of a Discord webhook URL authority to enter agent sessions, and `mapToUser` crosses authorization and session-identity boundaries.

options.title: Approve allowlist only
options.body: Allow a narrow webhook-id allowlist to pass the bot-message gate, while deferring or rejecting user impersonation until its authorization semantics are separately defined.

options.title: Approve allowlist plus user mapping
options.body: Permit `mapToUser` only with strict validation against configured guild users, clear audit/logging behavior, and tests proving it cannot bypass sender authorization or session isolation.

options.title: Decline Discord-specific webhook ingress
options.body: Keep Discord bot-message policy unchanged and direct external automation to a generic authenticated webhooks plugin or ClawHub integration instead of adding another Discord config surface.

recommendation.title: Approve allowlist only
recommendation.body: Allow a narrow webhook-id allowlist to pass the bot-message gate, while deferring or rejecting user impersonation until its authorization semantics are separately defined.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Discord preflight, inbound policy, and bot-loop history make this the best available routing candidate for the security/product boundary decision.
